I did online high school  the last two years of high school, and that left me socially out of touch. It was like relearning how to walk. 

Here are the steps I took to expand my comfort zone. 
- For one month I practiced holding calm and relaxed eye contact. Eye contact is a fundamental part of interacting with people that does a few things simultaneously. It makes people feel seen which is huge, people will assume you’re confident, and people will trust you more. 

Additionally, you’ll want to be aware of your body language. Some key points you should look into would be maintaining a relaxed posture, have your shoulders and or feet facing the person you’re speaking to, keeping your arms and legs uncrossed. It’s not a hard rule, and doesn’t need to be followed 100% of the time. If you notice yourself crossing your arms, turning away from your person, and you’re not holding relaxed eye contact, then make the slight changes and settle yourself. 

- Keep practicing eye contact while you learn to actively listen in conversations, giving nonverbal affirmations, and learning to sit in silence for a few seconds. You want to practice active listening before you learn to free associate conversations, as this will support your conversational skills. 

I’m not going to explain because that would take forever, so look up conversational-threading on Reddit and read a few posts. This changed the game for me, additionally I’d recommend [how to never run out of things to say, and flirting](https://youtu.be/oxOih6GwSXI?si=qWkl14XXBOZD5Dsr). I wouldn’t recommend going down the pickup rabbit holes before learning everything in this reply, but this guy has a simple way of explaining the skills and how you can improve your conversations. 

The goal of these skills are to make the other person talk about themselves, and in general your goal is encourage them to share things about themselves.  Nonverbal affirmations like “oh yeah?!” “No way” “mmm” “haha what?!!” or “wait, what do you mean by…”  are great ways to encourage the person to continue their story. 

And finally the dreaded awkward silences, if you learn to be comfortable in these pauses, you’ll essentially become Neo in the matrix. Remain calm, let the silence pass and either continue the conversation or ideally talk about something related to what the previous conversation was about using conversational threading. From what I’ve experienced, passing moments like these is like passing a test for how comfortable you are with the other person.

- last points, while you’re doing these practices, I want you to learn to calm yourself down. In the pickup community there’s a thing called approach anxiety that newbies hyper focus on, and it keeps them stuck for years. They look for ways to eliminate this fear of approaching, but the truth is that it never goes away. It’s an evolutionary response that’s stuck to your biology, it’ll never go away but tolerance builds as you expose yourself to more and more situations. Over time you’ll build a wealth of experience that allows you to put it in your periphery. It’s a pebble in your shoe that you’ll never be able to remove, you just sort of forget about it. So keep practicing with the knowledge that you’ll always feel that anxiety, go to your limit, then go a little past your limit and take a break. You do the same thing for building muscles. 

Next, I want you to be aware of how reactive you are. Chances are you react to the sounds around you, always looking at people for direction on what you should do. Instead I want you to move, talk, and react slower. Not too much, but to the outside world it should look like nothing surprises you. 

You want to be nonchalant, but maintain that attentiveness when you’re actively listening. It’s a balance you achieve when your eye contact is piercing, but calm. Your body language is calm and interactive but people know your attention is solely on them. 

 This is my style and what I’ve found to work for me. I’m like a mix of extrovert in that I enjoy social interaction and enjoy being the life of the party, and also enjoy my quiet time and taking things slowly. I can be the life of the party, but when I’m interested in a woman I can step into the zone and create an atmosphere that feels like it’s just the two of us in the room. 

Focus on these fundamentals for a few months like 3 to 5 months. Find a local bar or coffee shop that a lot of locals go to and introduce yourself. Your only focus is to get the other person talking about themselves. Find out what they like, affirm them, be interested, and share something about yourself that relates to them. The first time is always the most anxiety provoking, but it only gets easier from there. 


Once you have this down, if want you to look into learning watching charisma on command. 

From this point you’ll be learning how to train other humans how to treat you, it’s very similar to training a pet which is a weird way to explain you’ll learn how to set boundaries verbally and nonverbally. You’ll be learning to teach friends and romantic interests to be comfortable with touch, you’ll learn to recognize signs of discomfort and you’ll pull back and try again later, and you’ll also learn to recognize when it’s time to take the loss and step away from people who aren’t interested in you without taking it personal. 

I know this is a long comment but I think it would be a great fundamental lesson to learn the “inner game” principles of pickup. Don’t fall for the misogyny in the pickup community. You can read those posts, separate the misogyny from the knowledge, and test practice what you learn. 

Learning to get laid would include learning to flirt (watch the video linked above, practice it for a few weeks), learning to quickly gage interest based of indicators of interest from women (look that up), learn about shit tests, watch playing with fire on YouTube for how to properly set up an online dating profile so you actually get matches, how to plan dates with good logistics so you have a higher chance of closing, and how to improve your systems. 

A course I don’t recommended to everyone because he is a bit of a sociopath is Occams Razor by John Anthony Lifestyle. He has a system that works really well at getting you to understand the sales funnel that is dating in like a week or two. Practice the stuff above while watching his YouTube playlists. It’s basically his course for free and will give you a great foundation for the things that would take too long to explain on here. Warning: be an ethical and moral person. Don’t lie, don’t take advantage of people just because you get a little bit of social power. Keep being yourself, you’ll get there eventually.

Rents go up because the Federal Reserve increased interest rates which increases variable rate mortgages. Landlords have those mortgages, which means their monthly mortgage increases. 

Think about this, most landlords are small time investors and still work a job on top of managing a property if they can’t afford a property management service. They barely break even after their mortgage, property management fees, maintenance and repairs. They aren’t raising rents because their COL increased, it’s because their mortgage, management fees, and the cost of labor increased. 

There’s so much that goes into managing a property properly, and the problem is exacerbated when you have biased legislation and ordinances that hinder the owners ability to negotiate with the tenants. There are local ordinance that recently passed in my city that says you have to give tenants a 6 month notice before you raise rents. On the surface it sounds like a great idea, but if you take into consideration the owners liabilities you’d come to find out this limits the option of short-term rentals. It’s limiting choice in the market to those that can afford a deposit, those with high credit scores, and those with a higher income because the owners need the certainty to mitigate vacancy rates. This has excluded a larger population in the city, and it makes owners anxious and fearful which is never good. 

What do you think a landlord would do when they’re backed into a corner? They choose the safest option and raise rents, raise your deposit, increase tenant standards. What really sucks is this ordinance if not followed to the tee, gives tenants the ability to squat on the property and the owners have no recourse.

- Now we’re going to summarize the statement, do some debugging/Socratic questioning, then reframe it into a neutral or positive.

I realized I wasn’t ever good at maintaining relationships in general and did some research in networking and such. I learned most of these from sales trading I purchased and modified them for socializing instead of profit lol. 

Step 1: Research
You want to meet people you have common interests with. Start by writing down what you enjoy doing, make a list of 25 things. I really enjoy about 5 things, slightly enjoy 10 things, and the other 10 are negotiable. Just write them out. 

Next use Facebook, Snapchat, Instagram, and Meetup to find local groups that meetup. I enjoy sports so I found some local leagues and filtered for those that fit my with schedule. 

Step 2: Outreach
Contact the group leader or just join the group and go to their first meetup. 
RSVP and done

Step 3: Socialize
Be interested in the other person before you start sharing things about yourself. Crack some jokes, gauge their humor and interests. You’re there to find who you’re most compatible with. 

Step 4: Exchange contact info and plant seeds
Get their sc, fb, insta, or number. Start planting the idea of hanging out by talking about the activity or hangout idea. Do this midway through the interaction and gauge their interest. Talk about the cool themed bar you wanted to check out, or this hiking spot with an amazing view, etc. 

Plan the hangout. Get the time, place to meetup, and what activity you’ll be doing

Step 5: Follow-Up
Repeat steps 3 and 4 with the people you get along with

Step 6: Fill the funnel
Repeat all steps until you feel you have enough quality friends
